description: WE COME, WE SEE, WE DOOM
summary:
Speckle turns NISAR radar data into evidence of how the ground is changing. It reads NISAR GUNW and GCOV products from NASA Earthdata, fetching only the bytes it needs, and runs thirteen preprocessing steps, all visible in the interface. Users explore a 3D map with a timeline of ascending and descending passes.

Each calamity has its own independent pipeline. Seventeen are designed and four are live: earthquake, tsunami, flood and deforestation. The earthquake pipeline compares measured ground movement with a physical fault model (Okada) and can flag possible quakes missing from catalogues. Tsunami evidence comes from ocean buoys and a wave simulation, so a linked earthquake–tsunami event rests on two independent data types. Flood and deforestation pipelines track radar backscatter changes to show spreading water and forest loss. Results are ranked by strength of evidence, and the app says plainly when data is insufficient.

Planned work: tracing slight ground dents that reveal hidden collapse, river erosion effects on soil and vegetation, separating human-driven from natural forest decline, and radar changes before events.

The code is public on GitHub under an open licence. Its clear SAR insights make it a strong tool for data scientists and for planners.
details:
SPECKLE

repo: https://github.com/tech-doomsday/speckle

What is Speckle?

A global SAR (radar) hazard detection tool that ingests NASA/ISRO NISAR radar data and returns clear answers backed by evidence on how the ground is changing, tile by tile (10km MGRS tiles).

Main Sensor: NISAR (GUNW interferograms, GCOV backscatter from NASA Earthdata)

Backup Sensor: Sentinel-1

Provides status with evidence, never overstates probability

All steps in the process are visible (13 preprocessing steps).

Key Features:

Efficient Range Reading:

Only reads the bytes needed for a specific tile via HDF5.

13 Preprocessing Steps (P01-P13): Raw clips are transformed into one immutable SceneBundle via a series of 13 steps. This SceneBundle is content addressed and memory mapped.

17 Custom Independent Pipelines: Each pipeline is an isolated folder with their own manifest, preprocessing, fetching, model and decision code. We have 3 pipelines currently implemented, and working on flood, on correlations and impacts.

earthquake_coseismic (3.01): Okada elastic dislocation model with consistency check

tsunami_ocean_evidence (3.17): DART Buoy detection with shallow water wave modelling

deforestation (3.08): L-band CUSUM with cause attribution.

Transparent: Results are ordered by level of evidence. We are upfront when there is not enough data to make a decision. If we cannot fetch data then this is clearly stated as a reason.

Strictly Modular: An automated test stops pipelines from importing each other.

Deterministic: Seeding is done based on the content hash of the bundle. This means the same input will always produce the same result.

User friendly Interface: Includes cinematic intro video, 3D globe with timelines for ascending and descending passes, SAR overlays, earthquake observatory and background dashboards.

Flexible: Can be run locally using one script, via Google Colab for fast connection to NASA or can be deployed for free using Vercel + Render with Supabase caching our results.

Well tested: ~100 python test files, Playwright end to end tests and a CI guard to stop any science code getting to the browser.

Tech Stack

Engine: Python (3.11+), FastAPI, uvicorn, numpy, scipy, h5py, zarr, aiohttp, pyproj, shapely, asf_search, SQLite

UI: Next.js, React (19), three.js/react-three-fiber, GSAP, MapLibre, Leaflet, Recharts, TanStack Query, Playwright

Cache: Supabase (Postgres with row level security)

Files: 752 total (361 engine, 242 app-ui, 75 tests, 33 tools)

Hazard Pipelines

Designed Pipelines (17): earthquake, tsunami (ocean evidence, SAR coastal inundation), flood, deforestation, landslide, land subsidence, volcanic deformation, glacier ice flow, iceberg calving/drifting, permafrost thaw, wildfire burn scar, river erosion, coastal erosion, tropical cyclone, oil spill, urban damage.

Current Pipelines:

EARTHQUAKE (3.01)

Compares actual ground movement to a physical fault model (Okada 1985/1992). Compares nodal planes from literature and selects the best. Combines ascending and descending passes to maximise coverage. Can detect east/up movement if both geometries observe the ground. Can pick up quakes that may not be catalogued by fitting a source to the detected ground movement (UNCATALOGUED_CANDIDATE).

Live USGS ComCat events and ShakeMap corroboration.

Tsunami Ocean Evidence (3.17)

Uses two separate sources of evidence. Physics based model with Okada seafloor source, Tanioka-Seno slope correction, Kajiura filter and well-balanced finite volume shallow water solver (HLL, MUSCL, SSP-RK2). Eikonal travel times. Solver checks include lake at rest, dam break, Ritter front speed, wave speed and travel time.

Runs in its own heavy lane with progress and caching by content hash.

DEFORESTATION (3.08)

CUSUM change detection with persistence rule. Uses both stages of L-band (early HV-HH ratio and late HV drop). Adjusts for rain and moisture, ranks hotspots, dates each patch and attributes cause (fire, windthrow, clearing or unknown). Reference data adapters include GFW alerts, FIRMS fires, IMERG rain, IBTrACS storms and UMD tree cover loss.

Flow Charts

5.1 End to End

point/tile/event window

|

[retrieval] ASF/CMR search -> layout index -> chunk plan -> range read

| -> decode -> clip store

|

[common] P01 ... P13 -> SceneBundle (immutable, content addressed)

|

[registry] route (P12) -> gate -> lane -> pipeline run -> PipelineResult

|

[verdict] collect -> calibrate -> link_events -> select -> persist -> Supabase

|

[api] FastAPI :8900 <- polled by -> [app-ui] Next.js :3000

5.2 Retrieval

box + dates -> asf_search/CMR -> list of granules

-> layout index per granule -> chunk table for box

-> range read (parallel, gap fill, retry, stall timeout)

-> parallel decode

-> Caching (RAM -> disk -> clip store (zarr))

Earthdata token only sent to NASA/ASF hosts.

5.3 Common Preprocessing

P01: Granule resolution

P02: Clip

P03: Decode gate

P04: Grid harmonisation (80m, 20m)

P05: Geometry

P06: Phase -> LOS displacement (sigma, coherence, ionosphere floor)

P07: Correction audit (always recorded)

P08: Backscatter pre-processing (GCOV -> dB)

P09: Ancillary alignment

P10: Temporal stacking

P11: Stability mask

P12: Tile routing

P13: Provenance

5.4 Registry

Scan manifests -> create bundle -> P12 routing per pipeline

no -> NOT_APPLICABLE

unknown -> NOT_RUN (always reported)

yes -> gate on data depth ->

normal lane -> process pool with deadline per pipeline

heavy lane -> job runner with progress and result caching

All responses are validated against the manifest and converted to PipelineResult. A failure in one pipeline will not affect any others.

5.5 Earthquake Pipeline

run(bundle)

Select pair(s): window covers event or latest pairs in scan mode

Quality mask: finite LOS, coherence gate and valid unwrap

Far field referencing -> displacement and uncertainty

Detection: |disp| > max(3 sigma, 10mm, ionosphere floor) Clustering and null check

Events: USGS ComCat within pair window and ranked

Forward check: Okada LOS prediction. Both sides are referenced.

Pass if amplitude ratio 0.25

Decision: SUPPORTED | NOT_SUPPORTED | INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE | UNCATALOGUED_CANDIDATE | NO_SIGNAL

5.6 Tsunami Ocean Evidence

Trigger or best event -> Seismic check

Observations: DART buoy time series -> Detide -> Sigma trigger

Simulation: Okada source -> Kajiura filter -> Shallow water solver on ETOPO1

Compare per station (arrival +/-15min, amplitude x3)

SUPPORTED | POSSIBLE | NOT_SUPPORTED | INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE

5.7 Deforestation

Forest mask -> Early window referencing -> Rain/moisture correction -> Multilook -> Z-scores

CUSUM with persistence (Early & Late L-band)

Patches of >= 0.5ha -> Null check

Attribution (fire | windthrow | clearing | unknown)

Ranked hotspots with onset dates.

5.8 Verdict Cache

PipelineResult -> collect -> calibrate (status to tier) -> link_events -> select (best verdict per tile, transparent no decision) -> persist (verdicts.db) -> Supabase Cache (Verdicts can be opened instantly in UI, even if engine is offline).

Redo in UI -> POST /api/runs -> Recalculate -> Overwrite cached row.

5.9 Deployment Options

Local: run.bat (Windows) -> engine (port 8900) + UI (port 3000)

Colab: zip / notebook / single file hub -> Tunnel -> Local UI

Cloud: Vercel (UI) -> Render (engine) -> Supabase Cache

User Interface

--------------

/ Cinematic landing page with scrollable video over WebGL earth

/map 3D Globe with search, granule footprints, timelines, findings, scans and SAR overlays (Auto, Linear, dB scale, Opacity, Hover & Click pixel values)

/earthquakes Guided investigation with event, coverage, scan, trace, verdict, map, evidence & archive sections

/console Home page with simple console and engine status

/runs, /verdicts Run history and verdicts per bundle

/background Background dashboards for retrieval, preprocessing, pipelines and health.

Tools

Debug Hub (python tools/hub.py --open). 4 Tabs: Data retrieval, health, data

processing, pipelines. Runs the real engine path with a recording proxy.

Colab Package: Notebook, scan and serve scripts. Single file retrieval hub for browsing all layers as images.

Supabase migrations and CLI to manage featured areas on the globe.

Docs: Implementation plan, port design, readiness audit, Supabase cache guide and step by step free deployment guide.

Quick Start (WINDOWS)

Requires Git, Python (3.11+) and Node (20+).

curl.exe -L -o run.bat https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Tech-Doomsday/Speckle/main/run.bat

.\run.bat

Clones repo, creates python environment, starts engine (port 8900) and website (port 3000). Opens http://localhost:3000.

Add a free NASA Earthdata token (EARTHDATA_TOKEN in .env) to enable real SAR retrieval.
